units.function: Embedded-Postgres route tests for resolving user- and Company-scoped SecretRefs in Adapter environment tests and Claude login, including responsible-user presence, declarations and honest access-event consumer attribution.
units.dependencyDirection: Board actor context enters Agent routes; the real SecretService resolves encrypted user/company values and records SecretAccessEvents, while Adapter test/login implementations receive plaintext runtime config. Environment/Agent identity determines consumer attribution.
units.keyDataModels: User Secret definition/value/declaration, Company Secret/version/binding, user/responsible actor, Agent or Environment/system consumer, Adapter env user_secret_ref/secret_ref and SecretAccessEvent.
units.lifecycle: An acting owner can resolve a required user Secret by key for test-environment without a declaration; missing responsible user fails before probe. Company SecretRef remains supported. Access events honestly identify system:adapter_test or environment:<id>, real user actor and responsible user, never a fictitious Agent. Claude login fails until a declaration binds the user's definition to the exact Agent config path, then receives the plaintext value.
units.testAssessment: Five database-backed cases validate real encryption/resolution, responsible-human fail-closed behavior, Company compatibility, consumer attribution and declaration enforcement for login. Missing are cross-user/cross-Company denial, revoked/rotated values, purpose/expiry, probe output/log redaction, rate limiting, declaration version/digest, approval, value zeroization and consistency: test-environment intentionally bypasses declarations that login requires.
units.designRationale: Support user-owned credentials for interactive setup and runtime login while keeping audit attribution truthful about which system/environment consumed the Secret and avoiding fabricated Agent responsibility.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs consistent purpose-bound delegation of a human's credential to a Connector action; diagnostic endpoints must not obtain broader Secret access than production execution.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT responsible-user fail-closed behavior and honest consumer/actor attribution. Require a versioned UserSecretGrant for every use, including diagnostics, binding definition/version, consumer, config path, purpose, Work/test command, expiry and accountable human. Prefer execution-node lease injection and redact probe outputs. REJECT owner-by-key implicit resolution without declaration as an enterprise default.
units.responsibilityConflict: test-environment can consume a user's Secret solely from an acting-user context and key reference, while production-like Claude login requires explicit declaration. That creates a purpose/consent bypass. Audit truthfulness records who consumed it but does not itself authorize the access or prove the user accepted diagnostic use.
evidence: 81f47e70a6296fa9e4dd1855646641b0c42a6c2d feat(secrets): thread the acting user into user-scoped secret resolution (#10115)

units.function: Database integration test proving pending-hire Agent configuration is service-frozen and activation reapplies the approved configuration snapshot even after direct Agent-row tampering.
units.dependencyDirection: AgentService creates/freeze-checks the pending Agent; ApprovalService stores the requested payload and, on approval, applies that payload back through Agent activation and related budget/config persistence.
units.keyDataModels: Pending Agent identity/role/config/runtime/budget/metadata/permissions, hire Approval requester/decision/payload and activated Agent state.
units.lifecycle: Generic Agent and permission updates on a pending Agent return a structured 409 listing frozen fields. Even a direct database change to name/config/runtime/metadata is overwritten when the Approval is approved, restoring the request snapshot and activating the Agent.
units.testAssessment: One high-value integration case covers service mutation denial, permission denial, deliberate database tamper and full snapshot reapplication. Missing are tampering with the Approval payload itself, cryptographic snapshot digest, concurrent decisions, requester/approver separation, partial apply/rollback, Secret version changes, environment/package availability drift, rejection/expiry/cancel and audit evidence linking the exact approved bytes to activation.
units.designRationale: Close the approval-time-of-check/time-of-use gap so an approved hire cannot activate with configuration changed after the reviewer inspected it.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS requires every high-risk approval to bind the exact action/configuration digest and reject or re-review any drift before execution or Agent activation.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT frozen pending state and snapshot reapplication. Store an immutable canonical request digest plus referenced Instruction/Skill/Secret-policy/Connector versions, sign or hash-chain the decision receipt, enforce requester/approver separation by risk and revalidate dependencies at activation. Any drift creates a new approval revision rather than silently reapplying mutable JSON.
units.responsibilityConflict: The same board-user requests and approves in the fixture, and the mutable Approval payload is treated as authoritative without content digest or independent evidence. Restoring config protects Agent-row tampering but cannot prove the reviewer saw the exact activated external package, Secret version or data policy.
evidence: fc95699fdef5b1295a64904b3aa287713e26ff26 fix(server): enforce agent secret binding sync across lifecycle flows (#8307)

units.function: AgentService database tests for clearing an error status while retaining failed-run history, transcript events and runtime diagnostics, with terminal/pending state protections.
units.dependencyDirection: AgentService updates only Agent lifecycle/error fields; HeartbeatRun, RunEvent and AgentRuntimeState tables remain separate evidence/diagnostic records and are read back to prove non-deletion.
units.keyDataModels: Agent error/idle/terminated/pending state, pause/error reason, failed heartbeat run/log/result, transcript event and persisted runtime session/state/last error.
units.lifecycle: Only an error Agent transitions to idle and clears pause/error presentation fields. Failed run status, stdout/stderr/log reference, transcript and runtime session diagnostics remain intact. Idle, terminated and pending-approval Agents receive 409 conflicts.
units.testAssessment: Three strong integration cases cover evidence preservation and state preconditions. Missing are optimistic concurrency, active run/session cancellation, reason/remediation input, audit actor, organization-chain and credential revalidation, runtime-state quarantine versus reuse, repeated idempotent clear, error classification and retention/redaction policy for logs/transcripts.
units.designRationale: Separate clearing the current operational alarm from deleting forensic history, and reuse resume-like lifecycle protections for terminal or not-yet-approved Agents.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must let a human acknowledge/remediate a failed Agent without erasing evidence or accidentally resuming stale authority/session state.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT evidence-preserving state transition and explicit preconditions. Require expected version, remediation reason/evidence, accountable human and risk-based approval; quarantine old runtime session/credentials until Connector health, responsibility, permissions and data contracts are revalidated. Emit immutable before/after recovery receipt.
units.responsibilityConflict: The service does not record who accepted recovery risk or why the error is resolved. Preserved runtime session/state may still carry stale credentials or unsafe context and could be reused after the Agent returns idle without a new authorization boundary.

units.function: Embedded-Postgres AgentService tests for transactional SecretRef binding synchronization across create/update/pending activation, plaintext Adapter-key conversion and allowlisted static-lease metadata.
units.dependencyDirection: AgentService and SecretService share database transactions: Adapter config is normalized to SecretRefs, Agent rows and CompanySecretBinding rows are created/replaced/backfilled atomically, and runtime resolution later dereferences the binding.
units.keyDataModels: Agent Adapter config, Company Secret/version, Agent binding/configPath/versionSelector/required, projection class/allowlist key, pending activation and transaction rollback.
units.lifecycle: Agent create extracts env SecretRefs into required bindings; approved class-3 static leases persist allowlist metadata and unlisted classes abort creation. Literal Hermes gateway keys become encrypted Secrets plus persisted references. Updating Adapter config replaces bindings. Legacy pending activation backfills missing bindings. Invalid references roll back create/update and failed activation stays pending.
units.testAssessment: Nine high-quality database cases cover create/update/activation lifecycle, non-env config, plaintext non-persistence, runtime resolution, class-3 allowlist and transaction rollback. Missing are cross-Company Secret ids, concurrent updates/rotation, old binding revocation and active-run leases, version-selector drift, provider failure, duplicate config paths, audit/grant provenance, deletion/offboarding, projection expiry and proof that class-3 material is revoked from sandboxes/logs.
units.designRationale: Make Secret binding metadata a transactionally consistent derivative of Agent configuration, safely ingest common plaintext setup inputs and constrain long-lived runtime projections to explicitly reviewed use cases.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs Secret custody and projection contracts that cannot diverge from approved Agent/Connector configuration and that roll back atomically on invalid or unavailable authority.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT transactional extraction/sync, plaintext-to-SecretRef conversion, allowlisted projection classes, activation backfill and rollback. Bind to ConnectorInstance and Work/Data purpose, pin approved Secret version or explicit rotation policy, track lease expiry/revocation and active consumers, enforce tenant checks, and emit immutable grant/change events. Static leases should be exceptional and execution-node confined.
units.responsibilityConflict: Bindings describe technical delivery but not accountable grantor, purpose, approved Work or data-export scope. versionSelector latest can change the credential after approval without a new decision. Replacing database bindings does not prove old plaintext/leases were revoked from active runs or remote environments.
